misconceptions.testDescription: The module path matches the import path.
misconceptions.feedback: The module path and the import prefix must agree. A placeholder module breaks resolution outside the current directory.

misconceptions.description: Believing any module can import an internal package.
misconceptions.feedback: internal restricts imports to code rooted at the parent of the internal directory. Other modules cannot import it.
go.mod declares requirements; go.sum records checksums. Both are needed for reproducible builds.

sections.title: A module is the unit of versioning
sections.body: go.mod declares the module path and the Go version. Import paths inside the module begin with that prefix. The module path is also the identity that other modules use to require a version, so it must match the repository location.

sections.title: go.sum records integrity
sections.body: go.sum stores cryptographic hashes of module content. It is not a lock file that replaces go.mod; the two work together. go mod tidy adds missing requirements and removes unused ones, then updates both files.

sections.title: Internal packages enforce boundaries
sections.body: A package under an internal directory can be imported only by code rooted at the parent of internal. This lets a module share implementation details across its own packages without exposing them to other modules.
